items.titleEn: With franchise legends in crowd, Blue Jays deliver gritty comeback win
bodyEn: TORONTO -- Sometimes you hit three home runs and cruise to victory, other times you have to grind to give yourself a chance.
On Friday it was the former for the Blue Jays, and Saturday, it was the latter.
Toronto rallied from a three-run deficit to defeat the Mariners, 4-3, in the second game of a three-game series at Rogers Centre.
Seattle jumped out to a 3-0 lead after four innings before walks and a defensive miscue let the Blue Jays back into the game in the bottom of the fifth.
With one out, Mariners starter Kade Anderson allowed a single off the bat of Myles Straw and issued a free pass to Brett Bateman.

Reliever Eduard Bazardo then came on to strike out Alejandro Kirk, but followed it with walks of Vladimir Guerrero Jr. and George Springer. What should’ve resulted in one run on the walk to Springer turned into two when ball four skipped away from catcher Cal Raleigh, allowing Bateman to scamper home from second.
The Blue Jays would score two more in the bottom of the sixth on singles from Bateman and Kirk to take a lead they would never relinquish.
Bateman admitted the play at the plate was closer than he anticipated, but he wanted to try to make something happen given the situation.

“I was rounding third and I looked up and Raleigh didn’t have the ball yet,” Bateman said postgame. “There’s two outs, just trying to be aggressive. It worked out. Live and die by being aggressive on the base paths. As soon as I touched third, my head was looking at home.”

Since his arrival in the big leagues on Aug. 7, Bateman has been the spark plug atop the lineup the Blue Jays have needed. After going 1-for-3 with an RBI and a walk on Saturday, he’s now hitting .329 across 76 at bats.
On the mound, José Soriano recovered from a tough start to the game to throw seven innings. He surrendered three runs on five hits with two walks and six strikeouts.
The entire day got off to an emotional start as the Blue Jays honoured long-time player, manager and broadcaster Buck Martinez by enshrining him in the franchise’s new Hall of Excellence.
It created an atmosphere that players took notice of.

“It was great,” Bateman said about the energy in the stadium. “The ceremony was awesome. I’ve been here a month and I almost teared up. It just shows how strong the community and bond is. I want the building to be like that all the time, and they’ve done that. They give us that energy. It was a great team win.”
Manager John Schneider continues to be impressed with his young leadoff hitter and how comfortable he is with such little experience at the major league level.

“You don’t see that very often,” Schneider said of Bateman scoring from second. “He doesn’t take anything for granted. It’s what we’ve tried to grasp onto a little bit after the Trade Deadline with guys like him and trying to force the issue. I think that kind of re-energized everyone.”
With the Guardians losing on Saturday afternoon, the Blue Jays now sit 1.5 games back of the final American League Wild Card spot.
Schneider was happy with the way his team won two very different games from Friday to Saturday, but ultimately all that matters is coming away with a victory this time of year, he said.

“Every win is going to be important and every win can come in any way, shape or form,” Schneider said. “It starts on the mound, Soriano was really good. Every game is going to be different and good teams find ways to do it in different ways.”
items.titleZh: 蓝鸟在队史传奇面前逆转水手
items.summaryZh: 蓝鸟主场4-3逆转水手，Bateman关键跑垒立功，Soriano七局好投，距美联外卡席位仅1.5场。
bodyZh: 多伦多——有时候你打出三支本垒打轻松获胜，有时候你必须努力拼搏才能为自己争取到机会。
周五蓝鸟属于前者，而周六则属于后者。
在罗杰斯中心进行的三场系列赛第二战中，多伦多蓝鸟在落后3分的情况下奋起反击，以4-3击败西雅图水手。
西雅图水手在四局过后取得3-0领先，随后保送和防守失误让蓝鸟在第五局下半局回到比赛中。
一人出局情况下，水手先发投手Kade Anderson被Myles Straw击出安打，随后又保送了Brett Bateman。
后援投手Eduard Bazardo随后登场三振了Alejandro Kirk，但随即又保送了Vladimir Guerrero Jr.和George Springer。本该因保送Springer而只丢一分的局面，却因第四坏球从捕手Cal Raleigh身边弹开而变成丢两分，让Bateman从二垒跑回本垒。
蓝鸟在第六局下半局凭借Bateman和Kirk的安打再得两分，取得领先并此后再未让出。
Bateman承认本垒上的拼抢比他预想的更接近，但在那种情况下他想尝试创造机会。
“我绕过三垒时抬头看，Raleigh还没有接到球，”Bateman赛后说。“当时已经两出局，我只是想积极跑垒。结果奏效了。在垒道上积极跑垒，要么成功要么出局。我一踩上三垒，眼睛就盯住了本垒。”
自8月7日升上大联盟以来，Bateman一直是蓝鸟打线顶端的火花。周六他3打数1安打，贡献1分打点和1次保送，目前76打数打击率为.329。
投手方面，José Soriano在开局艰难的情况下恢复状态，投了七局。他失3分，被击出5支安打，有2次保送和6次三振。
蓝鸟将长期担任球员、主教练和转播员的Buck Martinez请入球队新设立的卓越殿堂，让这一天以激动的气氛开场。
这营造出了一种球员们都能感受到的氛围。
“氛围棒极了，”Bateman谈到球场内的能量时说。“仪式非常精彩。我到这里才一个月，差点就流泪了。这正说明了球队的社区和纽带有多么牢固。我希望这座球馆一直都有这样的气氛，他们也做到了。他们给了我们那样的能量。这是一场伟大的团队胜利。”
主教练John Schneider继续对他年轻的第一棒打者印象深刻，也被他在如此少的大联盟经验下还能如此从容所打动。
“这并不多见，”Schneider谈到Bateman从二垒跑回本垒得分时说。“他从不把任何事视为理所当然。这正是我们在交易截止日之后试图抓住的东西，让像他这样的球员去主动制造机会。我认为这让每个人都重新焕发了活力。”
随着守护者在周六下午输球，蓝鸟现在距离美国联盟外卡最后一个席位还差1.5个胜场。
Schneider对球队从周五到周六以两种截然不同的方式赢球感到高兴，但他表示，在赛季的这个阶段，唯一重要的是带走胜利。
“每一场胜利都至关重要，任何形式的胜利都不例外，”Schneider说。“一切从投手开始，Soriano表现得非常好。每场比赛都会有所不同，优秀的球队会用不同的方式找到取胜之道。”

items.titleEn: Blue Jays legend Buck Martinez inducted into Hall of Excellence
bodyEn: TORONTO -- Forty-five years ago, Buck Martinez got home from a run to find his wife, Arlene, with a bottle of champagne waiting. He’d just been traded from the Brewers to the Blue Jays, and all he could think of was, ‘That’s the best they could do?’

Saturday afternoon, Martinez walked onto the field at Rogers Centre to the loudest ovation this stadium has heard since the World Series. It’s his induction day to the Blue Jays’ Hall of Excellence, where he’s now the 12th member and will forever be enshrined as one of the most beloved figures in this organization’s history.

What a man, what a life, what a story. Martinez still remembers every detail of those early days. There was a deal to the Yankees that fell through, then he rode around with the Brewers as a fourth-string catcher until the Blue Jays came calling, looking for a veteran catcher to help the pitching staff and work with a young Ernie Whitt behind the plate. So much more was waiting for him, though. So many times over the years, he’s called that trade “the best thing that’s ever happened to me.”

“Baseball isn’t about stats, it’s about memories,” Martinez said, “and we’ve experienced a lot of great memories over the years. The city of Toronto has changed my life. This organization, the Toronto Blue Jays, has changed my life. You, the fans, have changed my life. As I enter the Hall of Excellence today, I do so with a heart overwhelmed with gratitude. Thank you for believing in me. Thank you for welcoming me into your family. Thank you for letting me tell the story of Toronto Blue Jays baseball.”

The stadium Saturday was filled with people who love Martinez in different ways, but aren’t they all the same? There were former teammates like the great Dave Stieb, then Blue Jays legends who played under Martinez as manager, like Carlos Delgado. Younger fans will know him as the voice of the Blue Jays, that unmistakable voice in your living room, night after night.

“Get up, ball! Get out of here!” Joe Carter shouted, doing his best impression of Martinez Saturday morning. “It’s the enthusiasm he has for the game, then the way he played the game and managed the game. Just being involved in baseball for all of the years he was involved in it, this is a great honor.”

Regardless of which image comes to mind when you first think of Martinez, though, it all comes back to the same place. He connects with people. Whether he’s catching, managing or broadcasting, something about Martinez connects with the player or fan on the other side, making them feel like they’re part of something.

“He’s been here for such a long time and meant so much to so many people,” said Jose Bautista. “Being the voice in so many households, that goes a long way and that stays with people. I’m very happy for him and I’m happy he’s going to be in the Hall with us.”

At the unveiling of the Blue Jays’ new Hall of Excellence Saturday morning, all of these baseball legends lit up when they were asked about Buck. Just like us, all of them have known Martinez at different stages of his legendary career. When he was traded to the Blue Jays, Martinez thought he was “at the end of the line”, but he played six more seasons up to 1986, playing alongside some of this organization’s greats.

“He was an awesome teammate and an awesome person,” Stieb said. “He had a knack to calm me down when things kind of got out of control for me. He just has this way to soothe you and get your focus back into the game, and forget whatever I was mad about.”

Then came his move to broadcasting. Martinez’s full name is John Albert Martinez, and Paul Beeston, always the eccentric, calls him “Albert”. When Martinez’s playing days finally came to an end, Beeston, sitting in that meeting, had an idea.
“Albert…” he said, “do you want to do TV?”

Martinez didn’t have any interest in it. He’d always been a player and that’s all he knew, so he politely declined. By the time he got home and told his wife about this, Arlene made sure that Buck picked that phone right back up and called Beeston. The rest is history, and as Buck likes to say, she was right again.
“He’s been a leader in spreading the gospel of baseball across the country,” Beeston said.

This moment is so rare because Martinez is so rare. Players of past and present, coaches, executives and media members are rarely unanimous on any topic, but Martinez transcends all of those labels he’s worn. He is, to everyone, just “Buck”. He’s the man who feels like your old friend, but just happens to be one of the most important figures in this country’s sports history.
“The only thing I would say to Buck is thank you,” said Vladimir Guerrero Jr., “and I love you, man.”
As Martinez spoke Saturday, players watched on and cheered, friends and colleagues wiped away tears. One last time, we got to hear it.
“Swing and a drive!” Martinez said. “Get up! Get out of here! I’m gone!”
items.titleZh: 蓝鸟传奇 Buck Martinez 入选卓越名人堂
items.summaryZh: 蓝鸟传奇 Buck Martinez 入选卓越名人堂，成为第12位成员。
bodyZh: 多伦多 -- 四十五年前，Buck Martinez 跑步回到家中，发现妻子 Arlene 拿着一瓶香槟在等他。他刚刚被从酿酒人交易到蓝鸟，他脑海中只有一个念头：‘他们能做的就这些？’
周六下午，Martinez 走进 Rogers Centre 的球场，收获了这座球场自世界大赛以来最热烈的掌声。这是他入选蓝鸟卓越名人堂的日子，他成为该名人堂的第12位成员，并将作为球队历史上最受爱戴的人物之一被永远铭记。
多么了不起的人，多么了不起的人生，多么了不起的故事。Martinez 仍记得那些早期日子的每一个细节。曾有一笔到洋基队的交易告吹，之后他作为酿酒人的第四替补捕手随队征战，直到蓝鸟找上门来，希望找一位老将捕手帮助投手阵容，并与年轻的 Ernie Whitt 一起在接手区工作。然而，等待他的远不止这些。多年来，他多次称那笔交易是‘发生在我身上最棒的事’。
“棒球不是关于数据，而是关于回忆，”Martinez 说，“这些年来我们经历了许多美好的回忆。多伦多这座城市改变了我的生活。这个组织，多伦多蓝鸟，改变了我的生活。你们，球迷们，改变了我的生活。今天当我进入卓越名人堂时，我带着一颗充满感激的心。感谢你们相信我。感谢你们欢迎我加入你们的家庭。感谢你们让我讲述多伦多蓝鸟棒球的故事。”
周六的球场里坐满了以不同方式爱着 Martinez 的人们，但这些爱难道不是殊途同归吗？有像伟大的 Dave Stieb 这样的前队友，还有曾在 Martinez 担任主教练时效力过的蓝鸟传奇人物，如 Carlos Delgado。年轻的球迷会知道他是蓝鸟的声音，那个每晚在客厅里回荡的独特嗓音。
“起来，球！飞出去！”周六早上，Joe Carter 尽力模仿着 Martinez 喊道。“这是他对比赛的热情，还有他打球和执教的方式。在棒球领域参与这么多年，这是一项伟大的荣誉。”
然而，无论你最初想到 Martinez 时脑海中浮现的是哪种形象，最终都会指向同一个核心。他能与人们建立联系。无论是担任捕手、教练还是解说员，Martinez 身上总有某种特质能连接起对方球员或球迷，让他们感觉自己是一个集体的一部分。
“他在这里待了这么久，对这么多人而言意义重大，”Jose Bautista 说。“成为如此多家庭中的声音，这会产生深远的影响，并留在人们心中。我为他感到非常高兴，也为他将与我们一同进入名人堂感到高兴。”
周六早上，在蓝鸟队新卓越名人堂的揭幕仪式上，当被问及 Buck 时，这些棒球传奇人物都喜形于色。和我们一样，他们都在 Martinez 传奇生涯的不同阶段认识他。当他被交易到蓝鸟时，Martinez 以为自己‘走到了职业生涯的尽头’，但他又打了六个赛季，直到 1986 年，与这支球队的许多伟大球员并肩作战。
“他是个了不起的队友，也是个了不起的人，”Stieb 说。“当我有些失控时，他总有办法让我平静下来。他就是有那种方式安抚你，让你把注意力重新集中到比赛中，忘掉我生气的那些事。”
然后他转向了解说工作。Martinez 的全名是 John Albert Martinez，而 Paul Beeston 一向古怪，总是叫他‘Albert’。当 Martinez 的球员生涯终于结束时，坐在会议中的 Beeston 有了一个主意。
“Albert……”他说，“你想做电视解说吗？”
Martinez 对此并不感兴趣。他一直是球员，他只知道这个，所以他礼貌地拒绝了。当他回到家把这件事告诉妻子时，Arlene 让他立刻拿起电话回电给 Beeston。剩下的就是历史了，正如 Buck 喜欢说的，她又一次是对的。
“他一直是向全国传播棒球福音的领军人物，”Beeston 说。
这一刻如此难得，正因为 Martinez 如此难得。过去的和现在的球员、教练、高管和媒体人很少在任何话题上达成一致，但 Martinez 超越了他所佩戴的所有标签。对每个人来说，他就是‘Buck’。他感觉像是你的老友，但恰好是这个国家体育史上最重要的人物之一。
“我只想对 Buck 说谢谢，”Vladimir Guerrero Jr. 说，“还有，我爱你，伙计。”
周六，当 Martinez 讲话时，球员们在一旁观看并欢呼，朋友和同事们擦去泪水。最后一次，我们得以听到它。
“挥棒，击飞！”Martinez 说。“起来！飞出去！我走了！”

items.titleEn: Blue Jays honor icons with Hall of Excellence
bodyEn: TORONTO -- The gold curtain pulled back to reveal the eight living members of the Blue Jays’ new Hall of Excellence, each of them a franchise icon.

From left to right stood George Bell, Dave Stieb, Joe Carter, Cito Gaston, Carlos Delgado, Jose Bautista, Paul Beeston and Pat Gillick. In the Hall behind them, lockers stood for the late Roy Halladay, Tony Fernandez and Tom Cheek. These 11 men have shaped the Toronto Blue Jays into the organization we know today, and Saturday afternoon in Toronto, they’ll be joined by the great Buck Martinez.

Located on the 100 Level of Rogers Centre, tucked in the right-field corner, the Hall of Excellence is now open to fans, the next step in the Blue Jays’ encouraging efforts to preserve their history and tell those stories while moving this organization forward.
This is what some of the Hall’s members and Blue Jays representatives had to say:
Joe Carter (1991-97):

“What we have left are our memories. It’s great to come back here, talk about baseball and see everybody. When we had the statue unveiling [in July], we lost our great closer, Duane Ward. Our time is very limited. You take advantage of that when you can see these guys like City Gaston and Pat Gillick, then Buck Martinez going into the Hall of Excellence. This is something you don’t take for granted. Tomorrow is never promised for us. To see these guys and be associated with these guys … it’s a great way to cap a lifetime of baseball.”

“This is awesome. Everybody here had such great talent. You’ve got to go out there, give it all and succeed to be here. This is an honor. It’s great that they’ve recognized that and we get our little day in the sun again.”
Jose Bautista (2008-17):

“It’s good to have reminders, right? The little Easter eggs here and there to remind you of the history and what’s happened here with the brand that’s been built over decades. Then, what it means to play Blue Jays baseball. That takes shape over time with the personalities, the style of play and the historical moments. I’m glad to be a part of this and add my little grain of sand to that. This is going to continue to happen. We’re seeing it live with the guys playing today, like Vladdy and others. I’m very happy for the organization, very happy for the fans.”
Carlos Delgado (1993-04):

“This is fantastic. It is so important to remember the history of our franchise. They talk about us as a ‘new’ franchise, but it’s 50 years. There are a lot of great players who have played on this field and [Exhibition Stadium]. Having an opportunity to show people where the Blue Jays come from, it gives the city and the fans an opportunity to identify with the franchise. They did a great job. This is a beautiful space.”
President and CEO Mark Shapiro:

“Thirty years ago, the Blue Jays established the Level of Excellence to recognize individuals whose contributions helped define this organization. Today, we are building on that legacy. The Hall of Excellence creates a permanent home for the stories, achievement and memories of the players and leaders who helped build this franchise and shape Blue Jays history … The individuals represented here established the foundation of this organization and we are proud to ensure that their stories will continue to be told for years to come.”
Manager John Schneider:

“It’s a really cool way to remind people of the history of the organization. It’s cool to see names and numbers up on the stadium, but you can’t really feel them or touch them. Being physically closer to it, the example you go to is obviously Monument Park at Yankee Stadium. It’s here, it’s displayed for people to see and to learn more about the [players]. I think this is great, and the statue of Joe Carter is great. Whenever fans or players can get closer to that, I think it’s really good.”

The Hall is rich with memorabilia, too, including stunning display cases for the club’s Gold Glove and Silver Slugger winners. Some of the artifacts are obvious, like bats and gloves, but then there are some gems, like Delgado’s notebook where he took intricate notes on pitchers, or the cigar boxes in Beeston’s display, perfectly capturing the one-of-a-kind character.
This space will now be open to fans at all times, and as the Blue Jays continue to expand this Hall and what it holds, fans will have a voice in voting for who is inducted next.
items.titleZh: 蓝鸟设立卓越殿堂致敬传奇
items.summaryZh: 蓝鸟队正式启用卓越殿堂，致敬队史传奇。
bodyZh: 多伦多——金色帷幕拉开，露出蓝鸟队新卓越殿堂的八位在世成员，他们都是球队标志性人物。

从左到右依次是George Bell、Dave Stieb、Joe Carter、Cito Gaston、Carlos Delgado、Jose Bautista、Paul Beeston和Pat Gillick。在他们身后的大厅里，储物柜代表着已故的Roy Halladay、Tony Fernandez和Tom Cheek。这11位将多伦多蓝鸟塑造成了我们今天所知的球队，周六下午在多伦多，伟大的Buck Martinez也将加入他们。
卓越殿堂位于罗杰斯中心100层看台，右外野角落，现已向球迷开放，这是蓝鸟队在推动球队前进的同时，保护历史并讲述这些故事的鼓舞人心的努力中的下一步。
以下是部分殿堂成员和蓝鸟队代表的话：
Joe Carter（1991-97年）：

“我们所剩下的就是回忆。回到这里，谈论棒球，见到大家，真是太好了。当我们在（7月）雕像揭幕时，我们失去了伟大的终结者Duane Ward。我们的时间非常有限。当你能看到像Cito Gaston和Pat Gillick这些人，然后Buck Martinez进入卓越殿堂时，你必须珍惜。这是我们不能想当然的事情。明天对我们来说从未有保证。看到这些人，并与他们联系在一起……这是为棒球生涯画上句号的好方式。”
Dave Stieb（1979-92年、‘98年）：
“这太棒了。这里的每个人都才华横溢。你必须走出去，全力以赴并取得成功才能站在这里。这是一种荣誉。他们认可了这一点，我们又能再次迎来属于我们的高光时刻，这太棒了。”
Jose Bautista（2008-17年）：
“有这些提醒是好事，对吧？这里那里的小彩蛋让你想起历史，想起几十年来建立起的品牌所发生的事情。然后是效力蓝鸟队意味着什么。这随着时间推移，通过个性、打法和历史时刻逐渐形成。我很高兴成为其中一员，为之添砖加瓦。这将继续发生。我们正通过今天打球的球员，如Vladdy等人，亲眼目睹这一切。我为球队感到非常高兴，为球迷感到非常高兴。”
Carlos Delgado（1993-04年）：
“这太棒了。记住我们球队的历史非常重要。他们把我们当作一支‘新’球队，但已经有50年了。在这片球场和Exhibition Stadium上打过球的伟大球员有很多。有机会向人们展示蓝鸟队的来历，让这座城市和球迷有机会认同这支球队。他们做得很好。这是一个美丽的地方。”
总裁兼首席执行官Mark Shapiro：
“三十年前，蓝鸟队设立了卓越荣誉榜来表彰那些贡献卓著、帮助定义这支球队的个人。今天，我们在此基础上继续发展。卓越殿堂为那些帮助建立球队、塑造蓝鸟历史的球员和领袖的故事、成就和回忆提供了一个永久的家园……这里所代表的个人奠定了这支球队的基础，我们自豪地确保他们的故事将在未来多年继续流传。”
主教练John Schneider：
“这是一种让人们铭记球队历史的好方式。看到体育场上的名字和号码很棒，但你无法真正感受到它们或触摸它们。通过物理上更接近它，你想到的例子显然是洋基体育场的纪念碑公园。它就在这里，被展示给人们看，让他们了解更多关于（球员）的信息。我认为这很棒，Joe Carter的雕像也很棒。无论何时，只要球迷或球员能更加接近这些，我认为都非常好。”
这座殿堂还拥有丰富的纪念品，包括为俱乐部金手套奖和银棒奖得主设立的惊艳展示柜。一些物品一目了然，比如球棒和手套，但还有一些珍品，比如Delgado记录投手详细笔记的笔记本，或者Beeston展柜中的雪茄盒，完美展现了其独一无二的个性。
这个空间现在将随时向球迷开放，随着蓝鸟队不断扩大这座殿堂及其内容，球迷将有机会参与投票，决定下一位入选者。

items.titleEn: Cease pads Cy case with yet another gem to right Blue Jays' ship
bodyEn: TORONTO -- The easiest way to forget an ugly loss that brought boos down from the home crowd? Hand the ball to Dylan Cease.

The ace was spectacular yet again, leading the Blue Jays to an 8-1 win over the Mariners to open their weekend series at Rogers Centre. With that, the Blue Jays are now 2 1/2 games back of the Guardians for the final Wild Card spot.
This is what mattered most:
1. Cy Young battle down to the home stretch
You could have predicted Cease’s line an hour before first pitch. Six innings, one earned run, eight strikeouts and another dominant performance.

The AL Cy Young race is down to Cease and Cam Schlittler of the Yankees, who countered with 5 2/3 scoreless innings (5 BB, 8 K) against the Red Sox Friday night. This could turn into a fascinating debate by the end of September, highlighting which statistics are valued most.

Manager John Schneider points to WHIP and quality starts as two of the more common metrics that he gives some added weight to. If he were running Cease’s Cy Young campaign, he’d highlight the reliability of Cease’s outings -- not just the dominance of his stuff -- and how rare this level of consistency is in the modern game.

“Just because of the way bullpens are used,” Schneider said. “When he’s out there, we’re pretty comfortable with him getting deep into the game. That impacts what you do in the days before and the days after.”
Cease has also struck out seven or more batters in 19 consecutive starts. The last pitcher to do that in a single season was Randy Johnson in 2001.
2. Add-on homers? The Blue Jays?
This is what it’s supposed to look like.

Both Nathan Lukes and George Springer tacked on solo shots to give the Blue Jays some extra cushion after they took a 3-1 lead in the first. These were both trademark swings, too, with Lukes dropping down to a knee to launch one out while Springer nearly toppled over, that all-effort swing connecting on a towering blast to left.

Watching that ball fly out, it immediately brought back the memory of Springer’s home run against the Mariners in Game 7 of the ALCS, which ultimately sent them to the World Series. We’re still too close to the heartbreak of 2025 for that moment to be fully appreciated and contextualized, but it will forever stand as one of the biggest moments in this organization’s history.

After that pair of homers in the fifth, Kazuma Okamoto joined the party with his 27th of the season an inning later. If the Blue Jays are going to pull off another run in September, power needs to be part of it. That’s a non-negotiable at this point, and it’s the Blue Jays’ only pathway to a winning streak longer than four games, which is their season high.
3. Vlad Watch: 11 home games remain

The box score will show an RBI double for Vladimir Guerrero Jr. and a flyout in his next at-bat. Oddly enough, that flyout was probably a more impressive swing, a line drive straight at the right fielder, while the double was a chopper up the third-base line with some good fortune behind it.

Either way, Guerrero has 11 home games left in the Blue Jays’ final 26, and he still hasn’t homered at Rogers Centre. Around the clubhouse and on the field pregame, Guerrero was loose and energetic, but of course he’s aware of this. After Friday’s win, his OPS sits at just .685.
The Blue Jays only have one shortcut to the final AL Wild Card spot, and it’s Guerrero.
items.titleZh: Cease再献佳作助蓝鸟回正轨，巩固赛扬奖争夺
items.summaryZh: 蓝鸟8-1胜水手，Cease六局失一分并送出8次三振，球队距外卡席位差2.5场。
bodyZh: 多伦多——想要忘记一场让主场球迷嘘声四起的糟糕失利，最简单的方法是什么？把球交给 Dylan Cease。
这位王牌投手再次展现超凡状态，带领蓝鸟在罗杰斯中心以8-1战胜水手，开启周末系列赛。由此，蓝鸟在争夺最后一个外卡席位时，落后守护者2.5个胜场。
以下是本场比赛最重要的话题：
1. 赛扬奖之争进入最后冲刺阶段
在首球投出前一个小时，你就能预测到 Cease 的表现数据：六局，一分自责分，八次三振，又是一场统治级表现。
美联赛扬奖的竞争目前集中在 Cease 和洋基的 Cam Schlittler 身上，后者周五晚对阵红袜投了5.2局无失分（5次保送，8次三振）。到九月底，这可能演变成一场有趣的争论，凸显哪些统计指标最受重视。
主教练 John Schneider 指出，WHIP 和优质先发是他更看重的两项常见指标。如果由他来为 Cease 的赛扬奖造势，他会强调 Cease 出场表现的可靠性——不仅仅是其球威的统治力——以及在现代比赛中这种稳定性有多么罕见。
“正因为牛棚的使用方式，”Schneider 说，“当他在场上时，我们很放心他能投长局数。这会影响到前几天和后几天的安排。”
Cease 已经连续19场先发至少三振七名打者。上一次有投手在单赛季做到这一点是2001年的 Randy Johnson。
2. 追加本垒打？蓝鸟？
这才是该有的样子。
Nathan Lukes 和 George Springer 各自击出阳春炮，为蓝鸟在首局取得3-1领先后增添保险分。这也是两人标志性的挥棒——Lukes 单膝跪地轰出一发，而 Springer 几乎失去平衡，全力挥棒将球轰向左外野的高飞本垒打。
看着那球飞出，立刻让人想起 Springer 在美联冠军赛第七战对阵水手队时的那支本垒打，那记本垒打最终将他们送进了世界大赛。我们离2025年的痛楚还太近，那个时刻还未被完全欣赏和解读，但它将永远载入这支球队历史上最重要的时刻之一。
在第五局那两记本垒打之后，Kazuma Okamoto 一局后也加入派对，轰出他本赛季第27号。如果蓝鸟想在九月再掀起一波连胜，长打火力必须成为其中的一部分。这在现在是不可妥协的要求，也是蓝鸟唯一能实现超过四连胜（本赛季最长连胜）的途径。
3. Vlad 观察：剩余11场主场比赛
技术统计将显示 Vladimir Guerrero Jr. 打出一支打点二垒安打，以及下一次打席的飞球出局。奇怪的是，那次飞球出局可能是更令人印象深刻的挥棒——一记直飞右外野手的平飞球，而那支二垒安打则是一记沿三垒线的内野弹跳球，带有一些运气成分。
无论如何，在蓝鸟最后的26场比赛中，Guerrero 还有11场主场比赛，而他仍然未能在罗杰斯中心击出本垒打。在赛前休息室和场上，Guerrero 看起来轻松而充满活力，但他当然也知道这一点。周五取胜后，他的 OPS 只有 .685。
蓝鸟要拿到最后一个美联外卡席位，只有一条捷径，那就是 Guerrero。
